title.value: Convergence of Proximal Point and Extragradient-Based Methods Beyond Monotonicity: the Case of Negative Comonotonicity
title.justification: The title accurately reflects the paper's focus on the convergence of proximal point and extragradient-based methods beyond the traditional monotonicity assumption, exploring negative comonotonicity.
title.quote: Convergence of Proximal Point and Extragradient-Based Methods Beyond Monotonicity: the Case of Negative Comonotonicity

extractions.description: The paper explores the convergence properties of proximal point (PP) and extragradient (EG) methods in optimization, specifically beyond the standard monotonicity assumption by considering negative comonotonicity. It provides complexity analyses, convergence rates, and constructs worst-case examples under this framework. The focus is theoretical, investigating convergence in the context of variational inequalities frequently arising in machine learning applications.

primary_category.justification: The paper is theoretical, focusing on mathematical convergence analysis of optimization methods. There are no direct applications or implications for eco-responsible fields such as climate change or sustainability.

applications.value: Theoretical analysis for optimization in machine learning models
applications.justification: The paper's focus is on developing theoretical frameworks for optimization problems that arise in machine learning, such as those seen in variational inequality problems (VIPs).
applications.quote: The study of efficient first-order methods for solving variational inequality problems (VIP) have known a surge of interest due to the development of recent machine learning (ML) formulations involving multiple objectives.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper delves into optimization theory, exploring convergence beyond monotonicity under negative comonotonicity assumptions. It provides mathematical foundations rather than eco-responsible applications.
new_primary_category.quote: Algorithms for min-max optimization and variational inequalities are often studied under monotonicity assumptions. Motivated by nonmonotone machine learning applications, we follow the line of works aiming at going beyond monotonicity by considering the weaker negative comonotonicity assumption.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The focus on convergence analysis of PP and EG methods under negative comonotonicity suggests a new sub-category more aligned with mathematical optimization theory rather than applications relevant to sustainability.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: In particular, we derive the first non-asymptotic convergence rates for PP under negative comonotonicity and star-negative comonotonicity and show their tightness via constructing worst-case examples.
